tier_reason: Repo is the SOSP '23 artifact (best paper) with full eval scripts for NOVA, PMFS, WineFS, Strata, SplitFS, OdinFS and ext4, and docs/main-claim.md states qualitative wins, but no numbers are on any opened repo page; the 3.1x-17x LevelDB and 1.3x figures come only from search snippets of the paper abstract (PDF host rs3lab.github.io blocked). Stays C until the paper is opened; a retier to B is likely once it is.

corrections.hardware: Paper: 8-socket, 224-core machine with Intel Optane persistent memory (docs/main-claim.md); artifact scripts timed on a two-socket 56-core machine; Ubuntu 20.04.4, Linux 5.13.13. CPU model not stated on opened pages.
corrections.caveats: Numbers quoted from search-result snippets of the paper abstract, not from an opened page (paper PDF host egress-blocked). Repo README and docs/main-claim.md give only qualitative claims; main-claim.md says ArckFS performs similarly to or worse than others below 56 threads (4KB) or 16 threads in FIO small-access tests, and wins mainly at high concurrency on the 224-core machine. A SOSP '25 follow-up (Analyzing and Enhancing ArckFS, KAIST with the Trio authors) found implementation bugs causing occasional operation failures and potential crash inconsistencies during inode creation; its patches reportedly keep the performance claims, but the bug-fixed code is not in this repo (see github.com/psb0623/trio-sosp23-ae). Optane PM is discontinued hardware. Artifact repo, 1 star, last commit 2023-08-24.

notes: Peer-reviewed source exists, so a paper-access retier to B is a candidate (QUEUE paper-access list). Bugs found by the SOSP '25 artifact study should be recorded as a shortcoming; per the later-fixed-code rule tier would stay capped at C anyway unless the follow-up re-measured.

First-party (LLNL authors) and unopened, so C.

corrections.caveats: Paper PDFs (osti.gov, arxiv.org, ieeexplore) egress-blocked; numbers quoted from search-result snippets, not from an opened page. Snippets confirm 1.22-1.9x over an optimized kernel-based service and 1.3x-1.6x rising with concurrency; the 1.25x-2.5x and Ligra 1.2-1.5x figures were not re-seen in this verification. Repo README has no numbers; applications live in LLNL/umap-apps. Default CMake build is Debug; use -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release. Needs userfaultfd (vm.unprivileged_userfaultfd=1 for non-root) and Linux >= 5.10 for read/write mode.

notes: Metadata matches (115 stars, LGPL-2.1, last commit 2026-07-21 on develop). Paper-access retier to B candidate once the TPDS paper (osti.gov/servlets/purl/1829975) is reachable.

tier_reason: docs/BENCHMARKS.md shows every claimed number (cp -r 22.7s vs 5.4s and 7.67s vs 5.14s on local NVMe; 60s vs 19s on GCP pd-standard; rsync 390s vs 165s for 9.7GB) with bench scripts in tests/perf, but CPU model, compiler and flags are not stated, so first-party C.

corrections.caveats: First-party numbers, apparently single runs; CPU model and compiler flags not stated; baseline is cp -r, not a raw read/write or io_uring baseline; speedup depends on many-small-file workloads (only 1.5x on 100K x 4KB locally). Network rsync baseline was run as rsync -az (compression on, SSH encryption) against uring-sync plaintext-protocol with kTLS AES-128-GCM; on 10K x 6KB (60MB) uring-sync kTLS was slower than rsync (2.98s vs 2.63s), and 34% faster at 589MB. kTLS + splice mode measured 2.9x slower than read/send in its own docs. Pre-shared-secret protocol, not a drop-in rsync replacement (no delta transfer).

notes: All numbers check out; GCP 3.2x row is ml_large (100K x 4KB). Metadata matches (4 stars, MIT, last commit 2026-01-07).
